```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The United States spends close to 17 percent of its GNP on health care.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Other advanced industrial nations spend 12 percent or less of their GNP on health care.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The health outcomes of the United States rank near the bottom of advanced industrial nations.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Private health insurers spend nearly one out of four of their medical dollars on marketing and administration.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Medicare’s administrative costs are only 3 percent of the program’s total expenditure.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A single-payer national health insurance system is the only efficient and just means to provide health care for all in the present political climate.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"With a single-payer system, private and non-profit provision of health care and consumer choice of primary-care physicians could be maintained.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The government would not take over the administration and provision of health care with a single-payer system.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A single-payer system would eliminate the wasteful and redundant private insurance industry and replace it with one insurer.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A single-payer system is equivalent to “Medicare for all,” and not just for the poor or the currently uninsured.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The cost savings in a single-payer program could extend coverage to all citizens.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A single-payer system would make labor markets more efficient, as workers would no longer worry that a change in employment might adversely affect their medical coverage.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The huge savings in administrative costs and elimination of wasteful insurance advertising in a single-payer system could be used to improve the quality of health care.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
